slides.title:
The first week of a takeover
is *collection*.
1 — Configurations
slides.body:
From every device.
Pulled the *same day*.

slides.title: Why not the backup
slides.body:
Usually a month stale,
and missing whatever
was done in a *hurry*.

slides.title: 2 — The change record
slides.body:
Twelve months of it.
Read for the *gaps*
as much as the entries.

slides.title: A quiet quarter
slides.body:
Rarely means a quiet quarter.
It means changes happened
where the record *doesn't reach*.

slides.title: 3 — Monitoring config
slides.body:
Not dashboards.
What's watched, with what
thresholds — and what *isn't*.

slides.title: 4 — The automation
slides.body:
Including the parts
nobody runs any more.
It says what somebody *tried*.

slides.title: 5 — The fear list
slides.body:
Things people won't touch.
Not a document.
You get it by *asking*.

slides.title: Why it matters
steps: The answers are specific: that switch, that rule, that site.
Fear is institutional memory in its least useful form.
Every item marks a *real event* somebody lived through.

slides.title:
Collect it while you're
still allowed to *not know*.
slides.body:
The first week is the only
week naive questions
are free.
